extracted.intended_audience: practicing patent attorneys, judges, and law students studying patent litigation procedure
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and equitable doctrines governing appeals, taxation of costs, masters' fees, bills of review/revivor, and auxiliary equitable bills (perpetuating testimony, discovery) in patent infringement suits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealability in patent cases without regard to amount
rubrics_metrics.description: That in patent cases an appeal lies without reference to the amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent cases are appealable to the Supreme Court regardless of the monetary amount involved (see cited cases). Exception: questions solely concerning taxation of costs are subject to amount limitations noted elsewhere (e.g., no appeal if costs in controversy are less than two thousand dollars).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits and security for appeals (general rule and supersedeas)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party aggrieved may move for an appeal within two years after entry of the final decree; but if the appeal is to operate as a supersedeas the motion must be made within sixty days and security be given by the appellant sufficient to cover the award, if any, to the prevailing party, with his costs and damages for the delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appeal does not operate as a supersedeas security should be required of appellant (twice the amount of costs the appellee may recover); if it does operate as a supersedeas security should cover twice the value of all that is to be recovered unless otherwise secured. Timing and amount of security affect whether execution/supersedeas is stayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality: decree not appealable until return of master's report
rubrics_metrics.description: A decree cannot be appealed into from until after the return of the master's report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decrees referring matters to a master (for accounts or damages) are not final and thus not appealable until the master's report is returned; interlocutory decrees and references have special timing consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-final decrees referring to master are not appealable
rubrics_metrics.description: A decree referring the case to a master for an account or damages, but not dismissing the bill or decreeing costs, is not a final decree from which appeal lies to the Supreme Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if a perpetual injunction is granted, a referral for accounting without disposition of the bill is non-final for appeal purposes (cited cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal as to costs: amount threshold and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal will lie to the Supreme Court on a question of costs, not involving the interpretation of the Patent Laws, only when the amount is over two thousand dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appeals concern only costs the usual amount threshold (e.g., $2,000) applies; patent-matter appeals more generally are not subject to the amount limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supreme Court will not consider errors not apparent on the record
rubrics_metrics.description: No error of law will be considered in the court above except those apparent on the record and duly and specifically assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errors not specifically assigned or not apparent on the record will be disregarded; appellants must assign errors with specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of evidence on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions of fact are heard and determined upon the evidence sent up with the record; or an agreed statement of facts may be submitted presenting the points on which the judgment of the court is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only matters in the record (including evidence actually sent up or an agreed statement) are considered on appeal; attempts to introduce new factual matter on appeal are generally disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collusive appeals and compromises during appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Collusive appeals are not tolerated; if, pending an appeal taken in good faith, compromises are effected between the parties so as to leave no real contest, the court will refuse further cognizance of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an appeal is rendered moot by private compromises that eliminate real controversy, the appellate court will dismiss or refuse to proceed; collusive conduct can lead to setting aside decrees of affirmance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement for appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: That notice of the appeal must be given to the adverse party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal notice is required (cases cited). If appeal is taken in open court at the same term no citation may be necessary; follow local practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record contents and what may be used on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: On appeal to the Supreme Court only the printed matters can be used at the hearing; the lower court should send up what was read or inspected below, not what was merely presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies should be sent up and originals kept in the court where they belong unless the court below believes originals need inspection above. Papers omitted from the transcript that ought to have been copied will not be noticed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficiency of a bare assignment that 'patent is invalid'
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment of error that the 'patent is invalid,' without pointing out the defect, is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments of error must state the specific defect or ground of invalidity relied upon; general or conclusory assignments are inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents and evidence not introduced below cannot be offered on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: On an appeal a patent not introduced below cannot be offered; affidavits taken before the master or the court below as grounds of application to open proofs cannot be taken as evidence on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters not presented to the trial court generally cannot be introduced for the first time on appeal; the appellate court examines the record as constituted below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supreme Court may consult record evidence to determine scope of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court may consult the evidence contained in the record in order to determine the scope of the invention, though prior use is not set up in the answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While new matters cannot be introduced on appeal, the court may look at the record's evidence to construe the invention and resolve issues of scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs in equity are discretionary and 'as justice may require'
rubrics_metrics.description: In equity costs are divided, awarded, or denied by the court as justice may require. They do not follow the judgment as a matter of right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prima facie the prevailing party is entitled to costs, but the burden rests on the adversary to show that such allotment would be inequitable. Courts exercise discretion and may depart from awarding full costs to the winner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of taxation of costs (final decree requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A full taxation of the costs cannot take place until final decree, and an appeal or supersedeas will stay the execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special costs may be allowed on interlocutory orders during proceedings, but final taxation awaits final decree. If the master reports, master's fee is payable on return and allocation may follow final disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs where plaintiff prevails on accounting issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If the plaintiff prevails in the issues raised on the accounting, the defendant must pay the whole cost; but where the defendant was willing at the outset to pay the net profits and the plaintiff has unnecessarily incurred costs, each party must pay his own costs and one-half the master's fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts apportion costs to reflect fairness and the parties' conduct; early willingness to compromise can limit cost awards to the plaintiff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs when master reports no profits/nominal damages
rubrics_metrics.description: When the master reports no profits or substantial damages, and nominal damages alone are given to the plaintiff, costs are allowed him up to and including the interlocutory decree, while the costs of the accounting are awarded to the defendant; one being set off against the other, and the balance recovered by the proper party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If plaintiff excepts to report and exceptions are overruled, costs allocation follows the circumstances; nominal damages generally lead to limited cost awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: No costs when neither party fully prevails or when plaintiff acquiesced to public use
rubrics_metrics.description: No costs will be taxed in equity when neither party fully prevails. No costs are taxed when the patent is found invalid and the bill is dismissed on the ground of the inventor's acquiescence in more than two years' public use or sale while ignorant of legal rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may deny costs where equitable considerations (e.g., acquiescence, both parties partially prevailing) make awarding costs unfair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Items of taxable costs in equity (typical list)
rubrics_metrics.description: The items of costs recoverable in equity are substantially identical with those taxable at law: the fees of the clerk, the marshal, and the witnesses, the cost of the pleadings, the expenses incurred for models or copies of models in the Patent Office, or for transcripts of assignments when procured by the defendant, and for necessary telegraphing, among others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also taxable: docket-fee (when final decree entered after replication), certified copies, certain printing costs for convenience may be disallowed; local practice and specific rulings (cited cases) determine other items. Depositions taken in another case and admitted by consent may not be taxed; solicitor fees may sometimes be allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket-fee rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A docket-fee is taxed in every case where a final decree is entered after a replication has been filed, and though several cases are by agreement heard together and one decree is passed deciding all, a docket-fee in each case may be awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a case is dismissed on motion of the plaintiff after issue and interlocutory decree on the merits, a docket-fee will be taxed. No docket-fee will be taxed for an attorney who did not enter on the docket before filing of the general replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on taxable printing and convenience expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The expense of printing evidence for the convenience of the court will not be taxed against the losing party; papers which ought to have been copied into the transcript and are sent up as originals will not be noticed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Printing or copying incurred solely for convenience may be denied as taxable costs; only necessary items tied to the record and evidence are generally recoverable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master's fees: payment, taxation, and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The master's fee is payable by the defendant on the return of the report, and may be recovered by him from the plaintiff if the bill is finally dismissed; the fees of the master are not to exceed fees allowed by statute to a commissioner in a like reference, though in some difficult or peculiar cases they may be greater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local district practice may vary (e.g., in Massachusetts master's fee initially charged to plaintiffs). The order of court for payment must be literally obeyed; the clerk cannot fix the master's compensation. The master is an officer entitled to compensation irrespective of the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: No attorney's docket-fee for attendance on reference to master
rubrics_metrics.description: No attorney's docket-fee is to be taxed for attendance on an order of reference to a master.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attorney docket fees are limited and generally not allowed for routine attendance on masters; consult local rules and precedents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of consent on taxation of costs and master's report
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs being once equitably taxed by consent, the consent cannot be withdrawn when the master's report comes in; and no costs will be taxed as to the exceptions to a master's report when all exceptions were overruled by the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties' agreements on costs are binding; exceptions to master's report that are overruled do not create separate cost awards unless the court directs otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bill of review — grounds and procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A bill of review may be filed, by leave of the court, for errors of law apparent on the record, and without leave of the court for errors in fact disclosed by the discovery of new evidence. When based upon errors of law it is governed by the same rules as a writ of error and must be filed within the time allowed for that proceeding; when intended to correct errors in fact it occupies the same position and is guided by the same rules as an application for a new trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts exercise caution in allowing newly discovered evidence; the bill must show new facts are material to some issue covered by the decree, that due diligence was used to discover evidence earlier, and that the decree would be different if the evidence were admitted. A decree by consent cannot be reversed on bill of review unless consent was obtained by fraud. Bills will be dismissed if petitioner was voluntarily absent or could have discovered evidence by diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bill of revivor — who may file and when
rubrics_metrics.description: When by death of either of the parties a suit in equity becomes abated, a bill of revivor will restore it. A bill of revivor can be filed only by or against the personal representatives, as distinguished from the assignee or devisee, of the deceased party, and only when the death does not prevent the court from granting the desired relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A devisee who cannot use revivor may file an original bill to obtain benefits of prior proceedings. A bill of revivor lies only where the cause of action would survive; specific procedural rules and equities apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bill to perpetuate testimony — purpose and use
rubrics_metrics.description: A bill to perpetuate testimony is required whenever it becomes apparent that on a future action certain evidence will be important, and that, though now available, this evidence may at that time be beyond the reach of the petitioner. Upon this bill the court will cause the testimony to be taken and preserved among the records of the court until needed at the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such bills are auxiliary to infringement actions where a proper plaintiff refuses to commence suit or cannot yet begin it. The court will only grant the bill where immediate suit is impracticable and the evidence is demonstrably at risk of being lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bill of discovery — basic definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A bill of discovery is a bill praying for the compulsory disclosure of certain facts within the knowledge of the [respondent].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text introduces bill of discovery as an equitable device to compel disclosure of facts; detailed procedural rules follow in the treatise (not fully included in the excerpt). Use when disclosure is necessary to the plaintiff's rights or preparation of suit.
